gate: n_eff > 2.0 required before claiming quorum value

cross_family_run_2026_08_04.note_on_legs: Three models from three different organisations. They share no weights, no training run and no architecture lineage.
cross_family_run_2026_08_04.finding: The pre-registered prediction in n_eff.py attributes the low n_eff to the legs sharing one 397MB blob. This run REFUTES that as the sole cause: three models from three different organisations, sharing no weights, still correlate at phi_bar +0.455. Architectural and vendor diversity is real and it helps — n_eff moved 1.19 -> 1.57 by adding a third family — but it does not reach the gate. Correlated error is therefore driven substantially by ITEM DIFFICULTY, not only by shared parameters: when legs err on 51-72% of items, overlap is expected even between independent systems.
cross_family_run_2026_08_04.consequence: Byzantine-fault-tolerance still MAY NOT be claimed. The retraction stands, and its stated cause needs widening: swapping in a different architecture is necessary but not sufficient. Raising n_eff above 2 likely requires legs that are individually STRONGER (lower error rates), not merely different — you cannot decorrelate three systems that are each wrong most of the time.
cross_family_run_2026_08_04.measured_on: RunPod RTX 3090 pod sov-brain-2, Ollama, GovBench DIMENSIONS, limit 40
